methods.sourceMethod: LIVE by Po-Shen Loh reference: place AC on the coordinate axis, locate B from distances, and intersect BP with the two required parallel lines. The vertex labels are chosen here so that D is nearer P.

annotationRationale: The main route converts the two trapezoid parallelisms into proportional lengths and then determines BP by the cosine law. Coordinates provide a distinct route through line intersections. The supplied Stewart calculation is another way to obtain the same needed length; the two retained routes offer accessible complete solutions.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The two parallelism constructions give PD=PB/2 and PE=2PB on the same ray beyond P. Independently, PB²=128, so DE=3PB/2=12√2, choice D. The two vertices give valid trapezoids, and the stem and key agree. Interchanging the names D and E is harmless.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: There are no shared-bank methods. The Random Math similarity/cosine route and LIVE coordinate route are both retained. Random Math's Stewart alternative is reasonably omitted: it repeats the same similarity reduction and replaces the short length calculation with a less familiar cevian identity, adding little learner benefit.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_p105 and cnm_272 appropriately identify the main geometric targets; cnm_055 supports AP=AC−PC and the segment subtraction. The route-specific cosine and coordinate concepts are supplied in the individual methods.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Both possible opposite-side parallelisms are covered. The stated triangle correspondences give PD/PB=5/10 and PE/PB=10/5. The included angle at C has cosine (225+196−169)/420=3/5, giving PB²=100+196−168=128 and DE=12√2.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: This accurately credits Random Math's first solution as a third-party basis. The direct PB ratios, explicit construction and expanded justification provide independent explanatory prose rather than a sentence-by-sentence rewrite.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why trapezoid conditions suggest similarity. The parallels, angle justification, point order and corresponding ratios are identified, and both cosine-law applications match the correct included angle.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p105 covers the trapezoid conditions, cnm_271 the AA similarity tests, cnm_272 the proportional sides, and math:general-cosine-law-application the two triangle calculations. All are used within their definitions.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native trapezoid and similarity topics apply. No accepted CN link is supplied for the general cosine-law application node.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-SRT.B.5 supports similarity applications; 8.G.A.5 and the quadrilateral-classification links supply partial components. G-SRT.D.10 and G-SRT.D.11 support the cosine-law portion, without demonstrating sine laws or their proofs. Transformation and slope links are not exercised; cnm_272 has no supplied US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All four nodes describe actual steps. The precise general cosine-law node correctly covers recovering a cosine from three sides and reusing it in another triangle.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Subtracting the distance equations correctly gives B=(33/5,56/5), and BP has slope 7. The required parallel lines yield D=(21/5,−28/5) and E=(9/5,−112/5). They lie beyond P, exhaust the opposite-side parallelism cases, and their distance is √7200/5=12√2.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The method accurately credits LIVE's coordinate construction and explicitly explains its swapped vertex labels. The added derivation of B and the intersection equations support the source-informed-original designation.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The coordinate placement is motivated, every nontrivial coordinate is calculated, and each trapezoid condition is translated into a specific line equation. The two-case list is complete and independently establishes the answer.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p105, cnm_h168, cnm_h172 and cnm_h173 respectively match trapezoid parallelism, equal finite slopes, line intersections and coordinate distances. Distinctness of the parallel lines follows from the nondegenerate triangle.
